name: FirstUK Bank — Complaint Handling Policy
description: The formal governing instrument for managing and resolving customer complaints at FirstUK Bank. It is owned by the Head of Customer Service and is applicable to all staff and customers.

name: FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints)
description: The specific section of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Conduct of Business sourcebook governing the handling of complaints.

name: FCA Handbook
description: The comprehensive set of rules and guidance issued by the Financial Conduct Authority that the bank's complaint handling must adhere to.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints), FCA Handbook

name: Head of Customer Service
description: The role designated as the owner of the Complaint Handling Policy, responsible for its maintenance and oversight.

name: All Staff
description: The collective of all bank employees who are designated as the target audience for this policy and are expected to adhere to its standards.

name: FCA
description: The external regulatory body that oversees the bank's compliance with complaint handling standards.

name: Customers
description: The bank clients who are the subject of the complaint handling process and a primary audience for the policy guidelines.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: A formal governing document establishing the bank's commitment and procedures for handling customer complaints fairly and efficiently. It covers the entire lifecycle of a complaint from receipt to regulatory reporting.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.
This policy establishes procedures for complaint receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Requirements
description: The regulatory requirements issued by the Financial Conduct Authority that govern the standards for handling customer complaints within FirstUK Bank.

name: Requirement for Fair and Efficient Complaint Handling
description: A high-level mandate requiring that all customer complaints be managed in a fair and efficient manner, ensuring alignment with regulatory standards.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.

name: Establishment of Complaint Lifecycle Procedures
description: A requirement to maintain formal procedures encompassing the receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting of customer complaints.
context: This policy establishes procedures for complaint receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting.

name: Compliance Risk
description: The risk associated with failing to adhere to FCA requirements regarding the fair and efficient handling of customer complaints.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: A governing instrument established to define the procedures for acknowledging, investigating, and resolving customer complaints fairly. It aims to ensure regulatory reporting to the FCA and the prevention of recurring issues to maintain customer relationships.
context: To establish complaint handling procedures that:

name: Prompt Acknowledgement of Complaints
description: A requirement that the bank must acknowledge all received complaints in a prompt manner.

name: Thorough Investigation of Issues
description: An obligation to ensure that all issues raised within a complaint are investigated thoroughly.

name: Fair Resolution of Complaints
description: A standard requiring that all customer complaints be resolved in a fair manner.

name: Regulatory Reporting to the FCA
description: A mandate to report complaint-related data or incidents to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) as required by regulation.

name: Prevention of Repeat Issues
description: An obligation to implement measures that prevent the recurrence of issues that have led to complaints.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The regulatory body to which the bank is required to report complaint handling activities.

name: Financial Conduct Authority (as Regulator)
description: The external regulatory entity responsible for receiving required reports regarding the bank's complaint handling.

name: Customer Complaints Policy
description: A formal governing instrument establishing the framework for handling customer complaints across all bank products and services. It defines the scope of application across all delivery channels and personnel.
context: Applies to: All customer complaints (product, service, policy)

name: All Staff
description: The collective of all bank personnel to whom the complaints policy applies, regardless of their specific department or function.

name: Customer
description: The subject of the policy who initiates complaints regarding products, services, or bank policies.
context: Applies to: All customer complaints (product, service, policy)

name: All Accounts
description: Any bank account held by a customer that may be the subject of a formal complaint under this policy.
context: Applies to: All accounts and products

name: All Products
description: Any banking product offered by FirstUK Bank that is covered under the scope of the complaints handling policy.
context: Applies to: All accounts and products

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: The governing instrument outlining FirstUK Bank's commitment to treating customer complaints seriously and ensuring fair resolution within regulatory timeframes.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously and resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: Fair and Timely Resolution of Customer Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement that all customer complaints must be resolved fairly and conducted within the timeframes prescribed by regulators.
context: resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The corporate entity responsible for the serious treatment and fair resolution of customer complaints.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously

name: Customer
description: The subject of the complaints process whose grievances must be addressed fairly and within regulatory timeframes.

name: Complaints Policy
description: The governing instrument defining how FirstUK Bank identifies and handles customer dissatisfaction regarding its services or products.

name: Customer Dissatisfaction
description: The risk arising from any expression of dissatisfaction by a customer concerning the bank's service or product offerings.
context: Complaint: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product.

name: Bank Customer
description: An individual or entity utilizing FirstUK Bank services who may express dissatisfaction through a formal or informal complaint.
context: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product.

name: FirstUK Bank Product
description: Any financial product offered by FirstUK Bank that may be the subject of a customer complaint.
context: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product.

name: Service Complaints
description: Risks associated with the failure of service delivery, including processing delays, inaccurate information, poor service quality, and system outages.

name: Product Complaints
description: Risks stemming from the incorrect application of product terms, including interest rate errors, fee mischarges, and misunderstood terms and conditions.

name: Financial Loss
description: Risks relating to the direct monetary loss of funds due to unauthorized activity, fraud, or administrative errors in balances and fees.

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A financial event where a transaction occurs without the account holder's authorization, leading to financial loss.

name: Fraudulent Activity
description: Transactions or activities characterized as fraudulent that result in financial loss.

name: Complaint Receipt & Logging Policy
description: A formal policy governing the channels and procedures for receiving and logging customer complaints at FirstUK Bank.

name: Immediate Logging of In-Person Branch Complaints
description: Complaints received in person at a bank branch must be logged immediately.

name: Recording and Logging of Telephone Complaints
description: Complaints received via the designated phone line (0800-555-2265) must be recorded and logged.

name: Immediate Logging of Email Complaints
description: Complaints sent to the support email address must be logged immediately.

name: Customer Portal Complaint Form
description: An online mechanism consisting of a dedicated complaint form within the customer portal to capture customer grievances.

name: Call Recording System
description: A technical control used to record phone complaints for logging and audit purposes.

name: Customer
description: The individual utilizing the approved bank channels to submit a formal complaint.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: A governing instrument defining the mandatory immediate actions and procedural requirements for recording, acknowledging, and logging customer complaints within FirstUK Bank.

name: Mandatory Complaint Recording Requirements
description: Staff must record specific data points upon receipt of a complaint, including date, time, customer identification, verbatim details, channel, and the receiving staff member.

name: Customer Acknowledgment Timeframes and Channels
description: Mandates specific acknowledgment protocols based on the communication channel: immediate verbal and written for branches, within 24 hours for phone, automated for email, and within 2 business days for letters.
context: Branch: Immediate verbal acknowledgment + written confirmation
Phone: Verbal acknowledgment + written confirmation within 24 hours
Letter: Written acknowledgment within 2 business days

name: Systemic Complaint Logging Obligation
description: Requires that all complaints be formally logged in the CRM system, assigned a unique ID, categorized, and routed to a handler.

name: CRM Complaint Logging
description: The use of the CRM system to maintain a centralized record of customer complaints, ensuring each is assigned a unique identifier and category.

name: Complaint Handler
description: The designated staff member to whom a logged complaint is assigned for resolution and management.

name: Receiving Staff
description: The employee responsible for the initial intake of the complaint and the recording of preliminary details.

name: Complaining Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of a complaint and the recipient of mandatory acknowledgments.

name: Customer Complaint Account
description: The specific customer account associated with a lodged complaint, used for identification and record-keeping.

name: Complaint Handling Process
description: A formal governing process outlining the steps for the initial assessment and triage of customer complaints based on severity and financial impact.

name: Initial Assessment Triage Timeframe
description: Mandates that the initial assessment and triage of a complaint must be completed within a window of Day 1 to Day 2.

name: Immediate Escalation of Urgent Complaints
description: Requires that complaints categorized as 'Urgent'—including those involving financial loss over £1,000, fraud, security breaches, service outages, or regulatory concerns—must be escalated to a Manager immediately.

name: Standard Processing of Low-Impact Complaints
description: Mandates that standard complaints, such as regular service issues, fee disputes under £1,000, or operational delays, are to be processed normally.

name: Fraud and Security Breach
description: Financial crime scenarios involving fraud or security breaches that trigger an immediate urgent escalation status within the complaint process.

name: Regulatory Concern
description: Complaints relating to regulatory concerns that are categorized as urgent and require immediate management escalation.

name: Financial Loss
description: Risk involving financial loss exceeding £1,000 which classifies a complaint as urgent.

name: Manager
description: The role responsible for receiving immediate escalations of urgent complaints, including those involving high financial loss or regulatory concerns.

name: Complaint Triage by Severity
description: An operational mechanism used to categorize incoming complaints into 'Urgent' or 'Standard' based on specific criteria such as financial threshold and risk type.

name: FirstUK Bank Investigation Policy
description: The governing framework defining the investigation phase of an incident response, specifically spanning Days 2 through 5. It outlines the mandatory steps for information gathering and documentation to determine liability and financial loss.

name: Mandatory Information Gathering for Investigations
description: Requirement that during the investigation phase (Days 2-5), specific actions must be taken including reviewing account records, checking transaction history, reviewing procedures/policies, interviewing staff, and assessing compliance.

name: Investigation Documentation and Loss Quantification
description: Obligation to formally record all investigation findings, identify the applicable policy or procedure, determine if the bank is at fault, and quantify any resulting financial loss.
context: Determine if FirstUK Bank at fault

name: Financial Loss
description: The risk of monetary loss incurred by FirstUK Bank resulting from an incident, which must be quantified during the investigation process.

name: Account Record Review
description: The operational process of reviewing customer account records to gather evidence during an investigation.

name: Transaction History Audit
description: The operational check of transaction histories to identify patterns or anomalies during an investigation.

name: Investigating Staff
description: Staff members involved in the incident who are subject to interviews as part of the information gathering process.

name: Complaints Resolution Policy
description: The governing framework for the resolution phase of customer complaints at FirstUK Bank, occurring between days 5 and 8. It outlines the potential outcomes based on whether the bank, the customer, or an inconclusive set of facts is at fault.

name: Compensation Obligation for Bank Fault
description: Mandatory requirement to provide full financial compensation for loss if FirstUK Bank is found to be at fault, including potential 8% per annum interest and additional compensation for distress.
context: If FirstUK Bank at Fault: Full financial compensation for loss
Plus interest (8% per annum) if appropriate
Plus additional compensation if distress caused

name: Apology and Process Improvement Requirement
description: Requirement to provide a written apology and implement process improvements to prevent recurrence when the bank is at fault.

name: Customer Fault Response Protocol
description: Requirement to provide the customer with an explanation of policy/procedure and supporting evidence, followed by a polite decline of compensation using an educational tone.
context: If Customer at Fault: Explanation of policy/procedure

name: Inconclusive Outcome Handling
description: Protocol for unclear cases requiring the bank to explain the evidence reviewed, acknowledge the customer's perspective, and potentially offer partial compensation or guidance on external ombudsman steps.

name: External Ombudsman
description: An external body referenced as a further step for customers when a complaint resolution is unclear or inconclusive.

name: Complaining Customer
description: The customer who has filed a complaint and is the subject of the resolution process, potentially receiving compensation, apologies, or educational explanations.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: A governing instrument defining the mandatory requirements for the final response stage of the bank's complaint handling process. It specifies the content, delivery method, and tone of the written response provided to the customer.

name: Mandatory Content of Written Complaint Response
description: A requirement that all written responses to complaints must contain five specific elements: acknowledgment, investigation summary, decision with reasoning, compensation details, and escalation rights.
context: Written Response Must Include: Acknowledgment of complaint, Summary of investigation, Clear decision and reasoning, Compensation offered (if applicable), Explanation of right to escalate

name: Complaint Response Delivery Standards
description: Mandates that responses be delivered via the customer's choice of email or letter, using plain language devoid of jargon, and maintaining a professional and respectful tone.

name: Complaint Response Deadline
description: Establishes a maximum timeframe of 8 days for the delivery of the final response to a complaint.

name: Customer
description: The recipient of the complaint response who has the right to choose the delivery method (email or letter) and the right to escalate the matter if unsatisfied.

name: Written Response Communication
description: The operational mechanism of issuing a formal written response (via email or letter) to ensure a documented audit trail of the bank's decision and the customer's notification of their rights.

name: FirstUK Bank Complaints Policy
description: A formal policy governing the response timeframes and escalation procedures for customer complaints to ensure compliance with FCA requirements.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Requirements
description: The regulatory framework and standards set by the Financial Conduct Authority that mandate specific response timeframes for banking complaints.

name: Simple Complaint Response Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to resolve simple complaints within 1 business day, with escalation to a Manager if the issue is escalated.
context: Simple (resolve quickly) | 1 business day | Manager if escalated

name: Standard Complaint Response Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to resolve standard complaints within 8 calendar days, with escalation to a Director if the matter remains unresolved.
context: Standard | 8 calendar days | Director if unresolved

name: Complex Complaint Response Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to resolve complex complaints within 8 weeks. This may be extended by a further 8 weeks if a complex investigation is justified and the customer agrees.
context: Can be extended 8 weeks if: Complex investigation justified, customer agrees

name: FCA Notification Obligation for Overdue Complex Complaints
description: An obligation to notify the Financial Conduct Authority if the 8-week timeframe for a complex complaint is exceeded.

name: Manager
description: The role responsible for handling escalations of simple complaints.

name: Director
description: The role responsible for handling standard complaints that remain unresolved within 8 calendar days.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The external regulatory body that must be notified if complex complaint response timeframes are exceeded.

name: Complaining Customer
description: The customer who initiates a complaint and must agree to any extensions of the 8-week response clock for complex cases.
context: Stops: When response sent to customer

name: Complaint Categories & Handling Policy
description: The formal framework governing how FirstUK Bank categorizes and resolves service-related complaints. It defines the investigation process, resolution criteria, and compensation limits for service failures.

name: Service Failure Risk
description: Risks associated with poor service delivery, including long wait times, provision of incorrect information, and unprofessional staff behavior.
context: Long wait, incorrect information, rude staff

name: Mandatory Service Complaint Investigation Process
description: Staff must conduct a thorough investigation into service complaints by checking timelines, reviewing followed procedures, assessing reasonableness, and interviewing staff where necessary.

name: Service Complaint Resolution and Compensation Requirement
description: When the bank is found at fault, it must provide an apology and financial compensation. Minor inconveniences are capped at £100, while higher amounts are mandated for significant distress or loss.
context: If at fault: Apology + compensation for inconvenience
Compensation: Up to £100 for minor inconvenience, more if significant distress/loss

name: Continuous Improvement Requirement for Complaints
description: The bank must implement process improvements based on complaint findings to prevent the recurrence of the same service failures.
context: Learning: Process improvement to prevent recurrence

name: Complaint Investigation Review
description: The operational process of auditing timelines and procedure adherence to determine the validity of a customer complaint.

name: Fee Disputes Policy
description: A formal governing instrument outlining the procedures for investigating and resolving customer disputes regarding bank fees, including unexpected charges, overdraft fees, and card replacement fees.
context: Resolution: If fee error: Reverse charge + interest

name: Mandatory Investigation of Fee Disputes
description: Staff must conduct a formal investigation for fee disputes by reviewing terms and conditions, verifying the correctness of the fee application, assessing the clarity of the disclosure, and reviewing the customer's history.

name: Fee Dispute Resolution Framework
description: Defines the mandatory outcome based on investigation findings: decline reversal if T&Cs are met, reverse charge plus interest if an error occurred, or refund with an apology if T&Cs were unclear.
context: If fee applied correctly per T&Cs: Explain and decline reversal
If fee error: Reverse charge + interest

name: Fee Dispute Risk
description: Risk associated with incorrectly applied fees or lack of transparency in fee disclosure leading to customer complaints and potential regulatory breach.
context: Example: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee

name: Terms and Conditions Review
description: The operational mechanism of cross-referencing the applied fee against the established Terms and Conditions to determine the legitimacy of a charge.
context: If fee applied correctly per T&Cs

name: Customer History Review
description: The process of assessing a customer's account history to provide context for fee application and dispute resolution.

name: Disputing Customer
description: A bank customer who has raised a dispute regarding a fee, such as an overdraft or card replacement charge.

name: Card Product Fees
description: Banking products subject to fee disputes, specifically relating to card replacement charges.
context: Example: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee

name: Account Balance Issues Policy
description: A policy section defining the investigation and resolution process for customer disputes regarding account balances, including missing credits and interest miscalculations.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations, Review any hold periods

name: Investigation of Account Balance Disputes
description: Mandatory investigation steps for balance issues, requiring the reconciliation of transactions, checking of system records, verification of calculations, and review of hold periods.

name: Resolution of Bank Error Balance Issues
description: Requirement to correct the account balance and provide interest on any missing amounts when a balance issue is determined to be a bank error.
context: If bank error: Correct balance + interest on missing amount

name: Resolution of Customer Misunderstanding Balance Issues
description: Obligation to explain and educate the customer regarding balance discrepancies when the issue stems from a customer misunderstanding, without applying penalties.
context: If customer misunderstanding: Explain (educate, don't penalize)

name: Resolution of System Error Balance Issues
description: Mandatory urgent escalation to the IT department to rectify the issue when an account balance error is identified as a system failure.
context: If system error: Urgent IT escalation to fix

name: Account Balance Discrepancy
description: Operational risk involving incorrect account balances, such as missing credits, wrong balances, or miscalculated interest.
context: Missing credit, wrong balance shown, interest miscalculated

name: Transaction Reconciliation
description: Operational control used to investigate balance issues by reconciling individual transactions.

name: System Record Audit
description: Control mechanism involving the review of system records to verify the accuracy of an account balance.

name: IT Department
description: The technical function responsible for fixing system errors identified during account balance investigations.

name: Disputing Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of a balance investigation and who may require education regarding their account balance.
context: If customer misunderstanding: Explain (educate, don't penalize)

name: Disputed Account
description: The account subject to balance reconciliation, interest calculation verification, and correction.
context: Correct balance + interest on missing amount

name: Disputed Transaction
description: Financial events that must be reconciled to determine the cause of a balance discrepancy.

name: Fraud Policy
description: The governing policy document specifying procedures for handling fraud and unauthorized transactions, including investigation and resolution protocols.

name: Fraud Investigation Process
description: Mandates a structured investigation process when a customer claims a fraudulent transaction, requiring the collection of statements, transaction reviews, authorization checks, and likelihood assessments.

name: Confirmed Fraud Reimbursement Timeline
description: Requires that if fraud is confirmed, the customer must receive full reimbursement and an apology within 10 business days.
context: If fraud confirmed: Full reimbursement within 10 business days + apology

name: Fraud Dispute Handling
description: Obligates the bank to conduct further investigations and follow FCA guidance in the event of a disputed fraud claim.
context: If disputed: Further investigation + FCA guidance

name: Financial Conduct Authority Guidance
description: External guidance issued by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) used to resolve disputed fraud claims.
context: If disputed: Further investigation + FCA guidance

name: Fraudulent Transactions
description: The risk of unauthorized or fraudulent financial events where a customer claims they did not authorize a transaction.

name: Fraud Team
description: A specialized unit responsible for conducting deeper investigations into suspected fraud cases when initial assessments require further scrutiny.

name: Claiming Customer
description: The bank customer who initiates a claim regarding a fraudulent or unauthorized transaction.

name: Fraudulent Transaction
description: A specific financial transaction that is subject to investigation due to a claim of fraud or lack of authorization.

name: Transaction Detail Review
description: The operational process of reviewing transaction details and assessing authorization to determine the likelihood of fraud.

name: Unauthorized Account Access Policy
description: Policy governing the response, investigation, and resolution of unauthorized account access and account takeover scenarios. It defines the mandatory steps for mitigating fraud and restoring customer security.
context: Customer discovers account used without permission

name: Unauthorized Account Access
description: The risk of a customer account being accessed and used without the owner's permission, categorized as account takeover.
context: Customer discovers account used without permission

name: Immediate Account Freezing for Unauthorized Access
description: Mandatory requirement to immediately freeze a customer account upon the discovery of unauthorized access as part of the investigation process.

name: Investigation of Transactions and Authentication
description: Requirement to perform a comprehensive review of transactions and authentication methods, including verifying if password changes occurred, following a takeover event.

name: Fraud Team Escalation and Law Enforcement Notification
description: Obligation to escalate the incident to the fraud team and, where warranted, notify law enforcement agencies.

name: Full Reimbursement of Fraudulent Transactions
description: The bank's obligation to provide full reimbursement to the customer for transactions identified as fraudulent resulting from unauthorized access.

name: Account Security and Access Reset
description: Requirement to reset account security and provide replacement cards or reset online access credentials following a breach.

name: Provision of Credit Monitoring for Identity Theft
description: Obligation to provide credit monitoring services to the customer specifically in cases where the account takeover involved identity theft.

name: Account Freeze Mechanism
description: Operational safeguard used to immediately prevent further unauthorized activity on a compromised account.

name: Authentication Review
description: Review process to determine if authentication credentials were compromised or changed during an account takeover.

name: Fraud Team
description: The internal collective responsible for handling escalated fraud cases and managing the investigation of unauthorized account access.

name: Law Enforcement
description: External authorities to be notified when unauthorized account access warrants legal or criminal investigation.

name: Affected Customer
description: The bank customer who has experienced unauthorized account access and is the subject of reimbursement and security resets.
context: Customer discovers account used without permission

name: Compromised Account
description: The customer account subject to unauthorized access and subsequent freezing and security resets.

name: Fraudulent Transaction
description: Transactions occurring without the customer's permission that are subject to review and reimbursement.

name: Replacement Card
description: The process of issuing a new payment card to a customer following a fraudulent account takeover.

name: Complaint Escalation Policy
description: A formal framework governing the escalation of customer complaints based on severity, financial value, and level of organizational involvement. It defines the authority and timelines required for resolution across different management levels.

name: Frontline Complaint Resolution Timeline
description: Requirement that simple, low-value complaints handled by Customer Service Agents must be resolved in less than one day.
context: Frontline | Customer Service Agent | <1 day | Simple, low-value

name: Manager Level Complaint Resolution Timeline
description: Requirement that moderate issues with a loss of less than £500 handled by the Complaints Manager must be resolved in less than five days.
context: Manager | Complaints Manager | <5 days | Moderate issues, <£500 loss

name: Director Level Complaint Resolution Timeline
description: Requirement that significant issues with a loss exceeding £500 handled by the Head of Customer Service must be resolved in less than eight days.
context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days | Significant issues, >£500 loss

name: Executive Escalation Timeline
description: Requirement that major failures or those posing reputational risk handled by the CEO or Board be addressed within a timeframe of 8 or more weeks.
context: Escalated | CEO/Board | 8+ weeks | Major failures, reputational risk

name: Complaint Escalation Triggers
description: Mandatory triggers that necessitate the escalation of a complaint, including unresolved manager reviews, financial compensation over £500, regulatory concerns, media/legal involvement, or FCA escalation.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The external regulatory body to which customers may escalate complaints, triggering a formal internal escalation process.

name: Reputational Risk
description: Risk associated with major failures or public-facing issues that could damage the bank's reputation, necessitating escalation to the CEO and Board.

name: Customer Service Agent
description: Staff responsible for the initial handling and resolution of simple, low-value complaints within a one-day timeframe.
context: Frontline | Customer Service Agent | <1 day | Simple, low-value

name: Complaints Manager
description: Role responsible for resolving moderate complaints involving losses under £500 within five days.
context: Manager | Complaints Manager | <5 days | Moderate issues, <£500 loss

name: Head of Customer Service
description: Executive role responsible for overseeing significant complaints with losses exceeding £500, with a resolution target of eight days.
context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days | Significant issues, >£500 loss

name: CEO and Board
description: The highest level of internal authority responsible for handling major failures and issues presenting significant reputational risk.
context: Escalated | CEO/Board | 8+ weeks | Major failures, reputational risk

name: Complaining Customer
description: The bank customer who initiates a complaint or escalates a matter to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

name: Compensation Framework
description: A governing framework detailing the financial compensation ranges and approval hierarchies for service failures and financial losses. It defines the basis for payouts and the internal authority required to approve specific payment amounts.

name: Service Delay Compensation Requirements
description: Mandates specific compensation ranges for service delays based on duration: £0–£50 for 1–2 days, £50–£100 for 3–5 days, and £100–£300 for failures exceeding 5 days.

name: Financial Loss Compensation Requirement
description: Requires the bank to provide full reimbursement of financial losses caused by error, plus an additional 8% interest.
context: Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest

name: Serious Distress Compensation Requirement
description: Specifies a compensation range of £250–£500+ for cases involving serious distress based on emotional impact.

name: Compensation Approval Hierarchy
description: Sets mandatory approval thresholds for compensation payments: Customer Service Manager for <£100, Director for £100–£500, CEO for >£500, and Board notification for amounts exceeding £1,000.

name: Operational Risk
description: Risks related to service delays and failures that result in operational disruption or significant impact to the customer.

name: Customer Service Manager
description: The role authorized to approve compensation payments less than £100.

name: Director
description: The role authorized to approve compensation payments between £100 and £500.

name: CEO
description: The role authorized to approve compensation payments exceeding £500, including those requiring Board notification.

name: Board
description: The governing body that must be notified when compensation payments exceed £1,000.

name: Affected Customer
description: The customer who experiences service delays, financial loss due to error, or serious distress and is the recipient of compensation.

name: FCA Reporting Policy
description: A governing framework defining the requirements for reporting specific categories of customer complaints to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

name: Financial Conduct Authority Rules
description: The set of regulatory rules issued by the Financial Conduct Authority that the bank must comply with and against which breaches may be alleged.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The external regulatory body to which the bank is obligated to report specific types of complaints.

name: Mandatory Reporting of FCA Rule Breaches
description: A mandatory requirement to report any complaint to the FCA that alleges the bank has breached FCA rules.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Mandatory Reporting of Financial Services Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement to report complaints regarding the provision of financial services to the FCA.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Conduct Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement to report complaints concerning the conduct of the bank or its staff to the FCA.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Financial Loss Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement to report any complaint that has resulted in financial loss to the FCA.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Systemic Issues
description: A mandatory requirement to report complaints that indicate systemic issues within the bank's operations to the FCA.

name: Compliance Risk
description: The risk of failing to report required complaints to the regulator, including breaches of FCA rules.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Operational Risk
description: Risks arising from systemic issues within the bank's processes that lead to reportable complaints.

name: FCA Reporting Requirement (COBS)
description: A policy governing the reporting of aggregated complaint statistics to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) under the Conduct of Business Sourcebook (COBS) framework.

name: Conduct of Business Sourcebook
description: The regulatory framework issued by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) governing the conduct of business for financial firms, including complaint reporting requirements.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The external regulatory body to which FirstUK Bank must provide aggregated complaint statistics and to which customers may escalate unresolved complaints.

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The entity responsible for the direct filing of aggregated complaint statistics to the FCA.
context: Who Files: FirstUK Bank (directly to FCA)

name: Quarterly Aggregated Complaint Reporting
description: A mandatory requirement for FirstUK Bank to file aggregated complaint statistics to the FCA on a quarterly basis.
context: Who Files: FirstUK Bank (directly to FCA)

name: Customer Escalation Right after 8 Weeks
description: A provision establishing that customers have the right to escalate their complaint to the FCA if the matter remains unresolved after a period of 8 weeks.
context: Customers can escalate to FCA if unresolved after 8 weeks

name: Aggregated Statistics Reporting
description: The operational process of aggregating complaint data for submission to the regulator, noted as not being automatically disclosed.
context: When: As data to FCA, not automatically disclosed

name: Complaining Customer
description: Bank customers who have filed complaints and retain the right to escalate to the FCA if a resolution is not reached within 8 weeks.
context: Customers can escalate to FCA if unresolved after 8 weeks

name: FCA Escalation Policy
description: A policy governing the process for customers to escalate complaints to external bodies when they remain unhappy with FirstUK Bank's resolution. It defines the communication requirements and the role of the Financial Ombudsman Service.
context: If Customer Unhappy: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information

name: Provision of FCA Contact Information
description: A mandatory requirement for FirstUK Bank to provide the customer with contact information for the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) if the customer remains unhappy with the bank's response.
context: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information

name: Escalation Letter Mandatory Content
description: A requirement that the escalation letter sent to the customer must include a statement of rights and the specific contact details (phone and website) for the Financial Ombudsman Service.
context: Escalation Letter Must Include: Statement of rights

name: Customer Escalation Time Limit
description: A rule specifying that customers must escalate their complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service within 6 months of receiving the final response from the bank.
context: Time limit: Customer must escalate within 6 months of final response

name: Financial Ombudsman Service
description: An independent body that provides a free service to customers for resolving disputes with the bank, whose decisions are binding.
context: Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)
FOS is independent, free to customer

name: Financial Ombudsman Service Representative
description: The independent entity responsible for reviewing customer escalations and issuing binding decisions on disputes.
context: FOS is independent, free to customer

name: Unhappy Customer
description: A bank customer who is dissatisfied with the resolution of their complaint and is entitled to escalate the matter to the FCA or FOS.
context: Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)
Customer must escalate within 6 months of final response

name: Complaint Data & Trends Policy
description: A governing framework establishing the requirements for tracking complaint data and analyzing trends within FirstUK Bank. It defines the specific data points that must be captured for every customer complaint.

name: Mandatory Capture of Complaint Tracking Data
description: A mandatory requirement specifying the exact data fields that must be recorded for each complaint, including date, type, category, customer details, outcome, compensation, and resolution timeframe.

name: Complaint Tracking System
description: The operational mechanism used to capture and store essential complaint metadata, enabling the bank to track outcomes and resolution times.

name: Complaining Customer
description: A bank customer who has raised a complaint, whose specific details must be captured as part of the tracking process.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: The governing framework for managing, reporting, and analyzing customer complaints, ensuring oversight from management, the Board, and the FCA.

name: Mandatory Monthly Management Reporting
description: A mandatory requirement to produce a monthly report for management covering total complaints, resolution times, upheld/rejected ratios, financial compensation, and trends.

name: Mandatory Quarterly Board Reporting
description: A mandatory requirement to produce a quarterly report for the Board focusing on volume trends, top complaint types, systemic issues, and corrective actions.

name: Mandatory Annual FCA Reporting
description: An annual reporting obligation to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) regarding aggregate statistics, effectiveness of complaint handling, and process improvements.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The regulatory body to which annual reports on complaint handling effectiveness and aggregate statistics must be submitted.

name: Management
description: The management layer responsible for receiving and reviewing monthly reports on complaint metrics and trends.

name: Board
description: The governing Board responsible for receiving quarterly reports on systemic issues and corrective actions related to complaints.

name: Complaints Reporting and Analytics
description: The use of periodic reporting (monthly, quarterly, annual) to monitor complaint trends, identify systemic issues, and track corrective actions.

name: Systemic Complaint Issues
description: The risk that recurring patterns of complaints indicate a systemic failure in bank processes or products.
